programme.thesis: Proposed strategy: earn relevant local attention through recognisable places, specific products and real work, then make the next menu, enquiry or shopping decision easier. There is no promised viral result.

phases.title: Establish the subject
phases.action: Confirm identity/routes/assets, capture the first distinctive process and place stories, and request an aggregated four-week account baseline.
phases.review: Read early questions and technical issues; the first small samples are descriptive, not proof of causation.

phases.title: Compare useful variations
phases.action: Run a small number of matched tests: local entrance versus food opening, sensory action versus explanation, useful comparison versus single subject.
phases.review: Compare like formats over equal seven-day windows. Keep trial, ordinary and paid distribution separate.

phases.title: Repeat what earns useful action
phases.action: Adapt the strongest evidence-backed subjects to winter meal, cake-enquiry and home-cooking decisions. Confirm any festive terms before adding them.
phases.review: Use repeated directional evidence and actual enquiries/bookings where attributable. Keep original hypotheses if data is insufficient.

programme.cadence: Planning assumption: 3 feed posts per week, 26 per client over the rolling two-month window. Each has a three-frame Story companion. Use a weekly source/production review; posting dates and slots are proposals, not accepted delivery commitments.
programme.measurement: Restaurant outcomes: qualified enquiries and verified booking completions. Retail outcomes: relevant product enquiries and voluntary source answers. Reach, watch time, shares, saves and link taps are separate signals, with their denominator and observation window.
programme.limits: All 182 posts remain drafts. Seven posts now have image-led carousel artwork and slide downloads; other entries remain copy and production briefs. The Feed view distinguishes actual visual drafts from Brief only tiles. No account scheduling, live status sync or client approval is implied. Sanitised planning data and explicitly requested draft visual previews are public; raw originals and private source records remain local.

strategy.goal: Build recognition of the Silverdale Road shop through familiar international pantry packs and useful browsing cues.
strategy.audience: Silverdale/Tunbridge Wells neighbours, diaspora shoppers and curious home cooks.

guidance.title: Original production
guidance.summary: Meta’s March 2026 Facebook guidance prioritises original production and can deprioritise low-value copies.
guidance.action: Film the actual venue, staff work and products; retain the source master. A border or speed change does not turn someone else’s footage into ours.

guidance.title: Account-specific Best Practices
guidance.summary: Instagram documents a Professional Dashboard education hub with personalised advice across creation, engagement, reach, monetisation and guidelines.
guidance.action: Check each client’s own hub before setting cadence. Our three feed posts per week are a proposed production baseline, not a Meta rule.

guidance.title: Trial Reels, where available
guidance.summary: Meta documents Trial Reels for testing with non-followers, with early metrics after roughly 24 hours and an optional automatic sharing decision based on the first 72 hours.
guidance.action: Check the actual Trial toggle and eligibility. Keep automatic sharing off unless explicitly approved; compare trial with trial, not with a normal follower-first release. No follower threshold is asserted here.

guidance.title: Music for a business
guidance.summary: Instagram’s Help Centre says its licensed music library is intended for personal, non-commercial use; some businesses have restricted access. Sound Collection is described as usable commercially.
guidance.action: Use recorded original sound without background copyrighted music, separately licensed audio, or an eligible Sound Collection track. Record the licence and placement; a trending sound being selectable is not proof of business rights.

guidance.title: Relevant captions and genuine responses
guidance.summary: Meta’s Facebook spam guidance addresses distracting captions, excessive hashtags, unrelated copy and coordinated fake engagement.
guidance.action: Keep the caption about the filmed food, place or useful decision. No comment pods, copied hashtag clouds or tag-three-friends bait. This does not set a universal Instagram hashtag count.

guidance.title: Collabs need an actual partner
guidance.summary: Instagram’s Collabs announcement describes co-authored content appearing across participating profiles once the collaborator accepts.
guidance.action: Propose one relevant local neighbour or supplier collaboration after checking fit, permission and disclosure. Do not promise doubled reach or contact a partner without authority. Current account limits must be checked in-app.

guidance.title: Edits is a production option
guidance.summary: Meta describes Edits’ clip timeline, watermark-free export, storyboards and feedback such as skip rate. Feature availability is account/device dependent.
guidance.action: Use a storyboard before effects, export a clean master, and inspect the first seconds. Installation or availability is not a tested client workflow; no client Edits setup is claimed.

guidance.title: Recommendation standards differ from mere permission
guidance.summary: Meta explains that content can be permitted on a platform while being excluded from recommendation surfaces.
guidance.action: Read Account Status and current recommendation guidance in the authorised account before release. A public profile review cannot establish recommendation eligibility.

guidance.title: Vertical export and safe areas
guidance.summary: Proposed house master: 1080×1920 for Reels/Stories; 1080×1440 for organic photo/carousel proofs, plus a 1080×1350 fallback if the scheduler requires it. These are production choices, not a claim of universal acceptance.
guidance.action: Preview the exact asset in the actual Instagram and Facebook publishing surfaces. Keep important text central and off interface controls. Current organic safe-zone pixels, scheduler support and maximum durations were not fully verified in this session.

guidance.title: UK and India clocks
guidance.summary: GOV.UK lists the UK clock change on 25 October 2026. Calendar slots use Europe/London; India is 4½ hours ahead before the change and 5½ afterwards, calculated with IANA time zones.
guidance.action: For 17:30 UK: 23 Oct = 22:00 India; 26 Oct onwards = 23:00 India. Recheck the actual scheduler’s displayed zone and final timestamp. No post has been scheduled.

guidance.title: A measurable experiment, not a viral promise
guidance.summary: Proposed learning cadence: compare the same format and similar duration over equal seven-day windows; change one variable per matched test and keep paid/organic and trial/normal results separate.
guidance.action: Record reach, average watch time where available, shares/reach, saves/reach and the defined action. Compare medians of at least four comparable observations when available; smaller samples stay descriptive. No invented performance target.

guidance.title: Commercial outcome definitions
guidance.summary: Client Insights, enquiry quality, till-linked footfall and confirmed booking attribution have not been inspected for this programme. Public counts describe the profile, not sales or content effectiveness.
guidance.action: Restaurants: count verified booking-system completions separately from link taps. Retail: use recorded stock enquiries and voluntary till-source answers with a denominator; do not relabel directions as visits. Missing data remains unknown.

guidance.title: Meta AI was consulted and checked
guidance.summary: Meta AI was asked for sourced UK local-business strategy in the browser on 21 October. It supplied useful leads alongside unverified limits, illustrative products and unsupported reach predictions.
guidance.action: Retain only independently read primary guidance. Trial follower thresholds, 20-minute limits, exact organic safe-area pixels, scheduler windows and doubled collaboration reach were not adopted as verified rules.

guidance.title: Photo size in the Instagram app
guidance.summary: The current Instagram photo-resolution article lists 1.91:1 through 3:4 for supported photo ratios and 320–1080 pixels width; at 1080 wide it lists heights 566–1440. The page was read in the browser on 21 October.
guidance.action: The first visual batch uses 1080×1440 PNGs as a supported organic-photo shape for the documented app context. Test the actual intended upload route; this does not certify every scheduler, API or ad placement.

guidance.title: Carousel order and shared orientation
guidance.summary: Instagram Computer Help describes up to 20 photos/videos in one post, one orientation for the carousel, and one post-level caption and location. Carousel videos are not Reels.
guidance.action: This batch contains three same-size slides per carousel, in a fixed numbered order. The dashboard previews each actual slide; it does not upload a post or prove route-specific API limits.

guidance.title: Alternative text for the actual image
guidance.summary: Instagram Computer Help describes replacing automatic photo descriptions with custom alternative text before or after sharing. The Accessibility input is part of the documented flow.
guidance.action: Use the supplied slide-specific alt text after checking the final image. Automatic recognition and a generic caption are not substitutes for an accurate description. No account upload was tested.

guidance.title: Reel media is distinct from its cover
guidance.summary: The current expanded Reel-size article lists 1.91:1–9:16, minimum 30 FPS and minimum 720px resolution. It separately recommends a 420×654 cover; that is not the master-video dimension.
guidance.action: Our future master choice is 1080×1920 at 30 FPS. A still image, carousel, animated thumbnail or storyboard does not count as a rendered Reel. Final grid crop and account upload still require testing.

guidance.title: Video captions depend on availability
guidance.summary: Instagram mobile Help describes speech-recognition captions and says captions may not be available to everyone. The computer-help variant was unavailable in this browser check.
guidance.action: Manually proofread speech, names and synchronisation. Caption availability is account/device dependent; do not confuse a post caption with timed speech subtitles.
